drafts.title: Improve front thigh support and match or exceed competitor rear legroom
drafts.description: Tall drivers must feel fully supported: the front seats provide noticeably longer thigh support when adjusted, and rear passengers have legroom that is not smaller than the main competitors in the segment.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Front seat cushion provides at least 60 mm of additional extendable thigh support compared with the current model when fully extended; in a three-competitor benchmark (the brand's established segment rivals), measured rear knee-to-seatback clearance is equal to or greater than the median competitor value in the benchmark protocol.
assumptions: Current-seat extendable cushion technology can be adapted to provide an additional 60 mm of effective thigh support within successor packaging.
Benchmark protocol and list of the three main competitors will be defined by product planning before validation.
Maintaining this packaging will not unacceptably compromise trunk volume or crash-structure requirements.
uncertainties: Exact competitor packaging numbers at launch; final benchmark targets may shift.
Interior packaging trade-offs (battery placement, NVH structures) could limit achievable seat extension.

drafts.title: Seat memory restores positions reliably and consistently
drafts.description: When a driver recalls a saved seat profile, the seat returns to the saved position quickly and repeatably so drivers do not have to readjust after the recall.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: On recall of a saved driver profile the seat reaches the saved fore/aft position within +/-15 mm, backrest angle within +/-1.5°, and lumbar within +/-10 mm, and the recall completes within 3 seconds in at least 98 out of 100 consecutive cold-start cycles during validation testing.
assumptions: Electrical supply and seat actuator hardware support consistent position control across temperature ranges.
Improved software logic and limits-of-travel calibration will be implemented to avoid cumulative drift.
uncertainties: Long-term wear or sensor drift could reduce repeatability; durability plan needed.
Interactions with multi-user profiles (key/fob vs. manual recall) must be verified.

drafts.title: Cup holders accept common bottle sizes and hold them securely
drafts.description: Drivers should be able to place commonly used bottles and travel mugs in the cup holders without wobble or needing improvised adapters.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Cup holders accept bottles and cups up to 95 mm in diameter (covering 1L water bottles and common travel mugs) and retain those items during a lateral bench test equivalent to 0.3 g without tipping or ejection.
assumptions: Standard test bottle diameters (e.g., 75–95 mm) will be used for validation.
Interior trim and center console packaging have available space to increase holder diameter to 95 mm if needed.
uncertainties: Increasing cup holder size may reduce available storage or require console redesign.
Some extremely large aftermarket bottles may still not fit but are outside the target range.

drafts.title: Hands‑free tailgate opens reliably on the first valid gesture
drafts.description: Customers can open the hands-free tailgate with a single natural foot/leg gesture reliably, without needing multiple attempts.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: The hands-free tailgate opens on the first valid gesture in at least 95% of attempts and completes the open action within 1.5 seconds from detection across a range of common footwear and gestures during functional tests (ambient temperatures from -10°C to +40°C).
assumptions: Sensing hardware and detection algorithms can be tuned to common footwear and motion patterns.
Validation will include a representative matrix of shoe types, gait speeds and luggage scenarios.
uncertainties: Interference from heavy clothing, crowded environments or tall bumper-mounted items may still require additional attempts.
Extreme cold or heavy ice may affect sensor performance outside the tested range.

drafts.title: Ambient lighting with a wide color palette and fine brightness control per zone
drafts.description: Customers can personalize interior ambient lighting with many colors and fine-grained brightness steps for each lighting zone.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Ambient lighting offers at least 64 distinct colors and a minimum of 10 brightness steps per lighting zone; users can select color and brightness independently for each zone in the vehicle UI and changes apply immediately.
assumptions: LED driver and software platforms used in the successor support at least 64 color presets and per-zone control.
The number of zones for independent control will be defined by the interior design team (typ. 4–8 zones).
uncertainties: Perceived color calibration between zones and materials may vary; harmonization effort required.
Additional zones or ultra-high color fidelity may increase cost.

drafts.title: Exterior door handles operate reliably in freezing conditions
drafts.description: Flush door handles must open reliably for customers in winter conditions without requiring manual de-icing or special tools.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: After exposure to -20°C and simulated ice glaze up to 2 mm thickness, door handles open on the first user attempt in at least 95% of tests (including wet/salt contamination scenarios) without manual thawing.
assumptions: Appropriate sealing, drainage or low-energy heating strategies are employed to prevent freezing adhesion.
Validation includes both static ice accretion and ice formed during drive cycles.
uncertainties: Extreme environmental cases (far below -20°C or unusual chemical contaminants) may still cause failures.
Trade-offs with aerodynamics or styling may limit some technical options.

drafts.title: Provide a usable 12 V power outlet in the trunk for portable coolers
drafts.description: Customers can power a portable cooler from the trunk socket for typical short trips without needing adapters or special wiring.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: A dedicated 12 V outlet is provided in the trunk within reach of typical cooler placement and is capable of powering a 40 W load continuously for at least 2 hours with the vehicle in accessory/off mode under normal battery conditions during validation.
assumptions: Vehicle battery and accessory-power policy allow providing at least 40 W for the specified duration.
Trunk layout will include a protected routing and fuse for this outlet.
uncertainties: Customer expectations for longer durations (multiple hours or overnight) are outside this target and would require larger battery or configurable accessory settings.
Outlet availability during certain vehicle modes (deep sleep) may be constrained by energy-management strategies.

drafts.title: Customer request: Front end to meet new EU pedestrian protection rules
drafts.description: Customers requested that the vehicle front-end meet the new EU pedestrian protection regulation.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This request is acknowledged; detailed regulatory compliance and implementation planning are managed by the regulatory/safety engineering stream.
assumptions: Compliance requires engineering design changes and formal homologation processes.
uncertainties: Specific compliance requirements and timelines depend on final regulation text and homologation schedules.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulation/homologation request — implementation and certification are handled by safety/regulatory engineering, so out of scope for customer-facing product requirements.

drafts.title: Customer request: Rear-seat airbag FMVSS 208 certification
drafts.description: Customers requested that rear-seat airbags obtain FMVSS 208 certification.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This request is acknowledged; certification and regulatory approvals are managed by the safety/regulatory teams.
assumptions: FMVSS 208 certification involves test programs and homologation efforts outside product-level feature definition.
uncertainties: Certification outcomes and schedules depend on test results and regulatory bodies.
drafts.scope_reason: Certification/regulatory request — out of scope for product requirement drafting.

drafts.title: Customer request: Headlights follow ECE R112 beam pattern rules in every market
drafts.description: Customers requested that headlight beam patterns follow ECE R112 rules across markets.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This request is acknowledged; headlamp beam pattern compliance decisions and homologation are managed by lighting/regulatory engineering.
assumptions: Regional headlight regulation harmonization and market-specific approvals will determine final implementation.
uncertainties: Market-by-market approvals and lamp supplier constraints may affect feasibility.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory/homologation requirement — out of scope for this product-requirement deliverable.

drafts.title: Customer request (engineering spec): Volume knob uses a 12-bit magnetic rotary encoder
drafts.description: Customers specified a particular component and resolution for the volume knob (12-bit magnetic rotary encoder).
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is an engineering-component-level request; component selection and resolution are decided by hardware/controls engineering.
assumptions: Detailed component choices belong to hardware engineering and supplier selection.
uncertainties: Trade-offs between user feel, cost and software smoothing may change component choice.
drafts.scope_reason: Specific component specification — engineering-level decision out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Customer request (engineering spec): Side windows with 4.5 mm laminated glass
drafts.description: Customers requested a specific glass thickness (4.5 mm laminated) for side windows.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This material/part specification is handled by NVH/glass engineering and architecture decisions rather than as a customer-facing product requirement.
assumptions: Glass thickness impacts NVH, weight and glazing supplier choices and must be evaluated by engineering.
uncertainties: Feasibility depends on glazing supplier capabilities and crash/passive safety implications.
drafts.scope_reason: Specific engineering/material specification — out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Customer request (engineering spec): Seat cushion foam density of 55 kg/m³
drafts.description: Customers requested a specific foam density for seat cushions (55 kg per cubic meter).
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a component/material-level request; final foam density and seat comfort tuning will be decided by seating engineering and validated in comfort benchmarks.
assumptions: Comfort is delivered by a combination of foam density, seat geometry and cover materials; final selection is an engineering decision.
uncertainties: Different markets and trim levels may use different material specifications.
drafts.scope_reason: Component/material specification — handled by engineering, out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Customer request: BMW guarantees a 60% residual value after five years
drafts.description: Customers requested that BMW guarantees a 60% residual value after five years.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a business/financial request that must be decided at the commercial/finance level and is outside product requirement scope.
assumptions: Residual value guarantees involve finance, resale market assumptions and risk allocation that are not product engineering requirements.
uncertainties: Market resale conditions and macroeconomic factors affect feasibility.
drafts.scope_reason: Commercial/price/financial request — out of scope for product requirements.

drafts.title: Customer request: BMW cuts production cost per car by 8 percent
drafts.description: Customers asked that BMW reduce production cost per car by 8 percent.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This operational/cost target is a manufacturing and business objective and not a customer-facing product requirement.
assumptions: Production cost reductions are achieved through supplier, process and program-level initiatives.
uncertainties: Cost reduction feasibility depends on supplier negotiations, volume, and program constraints.
drafts.scope_reason: Business/production cost target — out of scope for customer-facing product requirements.
